coverageEvidence.excerpt: Fictional splice-site example: 32 alternate reads among 160 usable reads give VAF 20 per cent. Suppose half the sampled cells are malignant, every cell has two local copies, and each affected cancer cell carries one altered copy, with equal recovery per copy. Then VAF = purity times cancer-cell fraction divided by two; 0.20 = 0.50 times CCF divided by two gives CCF 80 per cent. With pure cancer-cell input, the same 20 per cent fits CCF 40 per cent. These are model calculations, not counted cells. Local copy changes, altered-copy multiplicity, recovery bias or uncertain purity can change the fit. A measured splice junction and functional repair remain separate questions.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Replication makes DNA from DNA. Transcription uses a DNA template to make RNA. Translation reads the coding sequence of a message in three-base codons to build a polypeptide; the transcript and reading frame matter. Functional noncoding RNAs do not need to become protein. Reverse transcription copies RNA into DNA in relevant viral and retrotransposon contexts. This information-flow map is not a guarantee that every DNA change produces a measured RNA or protein change.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Variant-effect prediction estimates a specified consequence of a sequence change, whereas variant calling identifies changes from sequence data. Ensembl maps each allele of a variant onto every overlapping transcript with a rule-based approach, so the same genomic change can have a different consequence in different transcripts, and its impact categories (high, moderate, low, modifier) are qualitative assumptions about likely effect, not a measured loss of function (Ensembl documentation, release 116). A score from a missense tool does not answer a splice or regulatory question, and a prediction should name the reference genome, the alleles and the transcript (with its version) it was made for. A raw model score is not automatically a probability: a splice score of 0.92 on an unspecified scale does not mean a 92 per cent chance of lost function, because thresholds and evidence strengths belong to a particular tool and task. The absence of a prediction does not make a variant benign, because a tool may not cover that variant type or transcript. RNA junction evidence, functional experiments and clinical studies address different gaps, and none is interchangeable with a sequence score. Two reports of the same prediction from the same software version are two copies of one computed result, not two independent experiments. Where a tool's training data overlap the variants used to evaluate it, its performance can be overestimated, which is why the ClinGen calibration of thirteen missense tools to ACMG/AMP pathogenicity and benignity evidence strengths, estimated from local positive predictive value, used datasets assembled to minimise that circularity (Pejaver and colleagues, 2022). That calibration used ClinVar missense variants classified as pathogenic or benign and rare in gnomAD, within the ACMG/AMP recommendations for variants in genes associated with monogenic disease, and it selected no tool designed for splice variants. Its introduction notes that many methods overlap and so do not offer independent assessment of pathogenicity, which is why agreement between tools that share training data or inputs is not independent confirmation. The AMP, ASCO and CAP guideline for somatic variants notes that early prediction algorithms were developed and validated for germline variants and recommends that their results never be used as the sole evidence for variant classification or clinical decision making (Li and colleagues, 2017).

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
A driver alteration contributes to cancer development in a specified biological context. Vogelstein and colleagues' 2013 review distinguished mutations conferring a selective growth advantage from passengers without that advantage. Calling a sequence change reliably does not establish which role it has, and a familiar gene can contain alterations with different or uncertain effects.

Contribution to cancer development, current survival dependence and clinical actionability are different claims. The SHIVA randomised study did not establish superior progression-free survival for its particular pathway-matching strategy in refractory advanced cancer; that result limits the tested strategy without invalidating every precision treatment. Specify the alteration, measured function, disease and treatment setting, intervention, comparator and outcome before concluding that a drug will help.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A traceable finding identifies the specimen and assay, reference sequence with its version, genomic location and alleles, relevant transcript with its version, and supporting evidence. DNA means deoxyribonucleic acid and RNA means ribonucleic acid. A reference genome is the comparison sequence; a transcript is an RNA message. For a coding transcript, the annotated start codon fixes the coding frame, so the same genomic change can have different consequences in different transcripts. Not every transcript has a coding sequence. HGVS distinguishes experimentally observed RNA or protein changes from predicted consequences, conventionally putting predicted protein consequences in parentheses. A predicted splice effect is not a measured RNA junction, and a coordinate without its reference cannot safely join two reports.
coverageEvidence.sourceScope: Complete selected blocks read; block texts and hashes retained separately.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Variant-effect prediction estimates a specified consequence of a sequence change, whereas variant calling identifies changes from sequence data. Ensembl maps each allele of a variant onto every overlapping transcript with a rule-based approach, so the same genomic change can have a different consequence in different transcripts, and its impact categories (high, moderate, low, modifier) are qualitative assumptions about likely effect, not a measured loss of function (Ensembl documentation, release 116). A score from a missense tool does not answer a splice or regulatory question, and a prediction should name the reference genome, the alleles and the transcript (with its version) it was made for. A raw model score is not automatically a probability: a splice score of 0.92 on an unspecified scale does not mean a 92 per cent chance of lost function, because thresholds and evidence strengths belong to a particular tool and task. The absence of a prediction does not make a variant benign, because a tool may not cover that variant type or transcript. RNA junction evidence, functional experiments and clinical studies address different gaps, and none is interchangeable with a sequence score. Two reports of the same prediction from the same software version are two copies of one computed result, not two independent experiments. Where a tool's training data overlap the variants used to evaluate it, its performance can be overestimated, which is why the ClinGen calibration of thirteen missense tools to ACMG/AMP pathogenicity and benignity evidence strengths, estimated from local positive predictive value, used datasets assembled to minimise that circularity (Pejaver and colleagues, 2022). That calibration used ClinVar missense variants classified as pathogenic or benign and rare in gnomAD, within the ACMG/AMP recommendations for variants in genes associated with monogenic disease, and it selected no tool designed for splice variants. Its introduction notes that many methods overlap and so do not offer independent assessment of pathogenicity, which is why agreement between tools that share training data or inputs is not independent confirmation. The AMP, ASCO and CAP guideline for somatic variants notes that early prediction algorithms were developed and validated for germline variants and recommends that their results never be used as the sole evidence for variant classification or clinical decision making (Li and colleagues, 2017).

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
A repair-gene finding suggests a possible cause, a genomic scar records accumulated consequences, and a functional assay tests present behavior. A variant is not automatically damaging, loss of one copy is not automatically loss of both, and repair can recover while historical scars persist. None of these observations alone is the probability of clinical benefit.

Homologous recombination uses sufficiently matching DNA, often the sister chromatid after copying, to repair certain breaks. BRCA1 helps coordinate repair; BRCA2 helps RAD51 assemble on prepared single-stranded DNA to search and pair with a template. Template availability and cell-cycle state matter. In a fictional model with both functional BRCA2 copies lost, template-guided repair is impaired and alternative joining can leave deletions and rearrangements, but the sequence of a scar does not uniquely identify the cause or every protein that acted.

A low RAD51-focus count is interpretable only with adequate tumor cells, an appropriate cycling population and evidence that the cells experienced damage. Cruz 2018 assessed RAD51 with geminin as an S/G2 marker and gamma-H2AX as a damage marker in patient-derived models and retrospective tumor specimens. Fixed tissue can support this functional-surrogate approach; functional does not always mean live drug culture. An inadequate sample is uninformative, and a research assay needs analytical and clinical validation for its intended use.

Telli tested scar-score associations with response to platinum-containing chemotherapy before surgery in triple-negative breast cancer; that result does not establish a universal PARP-inhibitor cutoff. Farmer demonstrated sensitivity to PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cell models, a separate evidence setting. coverageEvidence.excerpt: Biallelic inactivation concerns whether either parental contribution still supplies useful function in the relevant cancer-cell population, rather than simply counting two physical DNA copies or two events somewhere in a tissue. coverageEvidence.excerpt: Genomic scars are historical patterns in sampled tumor DNA. Counts are not percentages of cells whose repair has failed.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Sequencing and functional testing answer different questions. A tissue or plasma assay needs coverage around the original variant, suitable deletion and splice-change detection, and a way to assess whether the changes share an allele; a hotspot-only panel can miss such events. RNA, protein or functional work may be needed for a proposed splice rescue. In Waks's RAD51 method, more than three nuclear foci in at least one cell across three examined fields supported repair proficiency, with geminin and control samples used for interpretation. A negative-foci sample with too few proliferating cells was uninterpretable. A visible focus alone does not establish completed repair, and a single RAD51 method cannot substitute for all sequence and clinical evidence.

RAD51 nuclear foci are assemblies of a protein involved in homologous recombination. Their interpretation depends on the sampled tumour cells, cell-cycle state, damage, staining, scoring and controls. A low count without enough informative cycling cells is uninformative rather than proof that repair is absent. The assay is a functional surrogate, not direct observation of every completed repair event.

Cruz and colleagues in 2018 assessed RAD51 with geminin as an S/G2 marker and gamma-H2AX as a damage marker in patient-derived breast cancer models and retrospective tumour specimens. Castroviejo-Bermejo and colleagues separately compared RAD51 and genomic HRD scores against olaparib response in breast cancer xenografts, then assessed feasibility in archival breast samples, including PALB2-related cancers. The latter clinical samples established feasibility, rather than a randomised benefit from choosing treatment with the assay.

A scar records accumulated genomic changes; a suitably controlled RAD51 result asks about a present repair-related state. Repair-restoring changes and acquired foci were observed in selected resistant BRCA-mutated breast cancers, but those small cohorts do not establish a universal treatment-switch rule. Use the actual assay version, informative-cell requirements and intended-use validation. A research score cannot replace the biomarker, disease and companion-test conditions of a medicine's label.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: PARP means poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase, a protein family involved in cellular signalling and repair. PARP1 is one representative. At damaged DNA it can build signals on proteins from chains of the chemical unit ADP-ribose, called poly(ADP-ribose), or PAR. Catalytic inhibition reduces this output. Some inhibitors can also stabilise DNA-associated PARP complexes, often called trapping. A repair-worker analogy separates a reduced call for help from a worker remaining in a doorway; proteins and medicines have no purpose, and the cell has more than one response route.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A DNA-associated protein obstacle can challenge copying without every encounter becoming a measured collision, double-strand break or cell death. Farmer 2005 demonstrated increased sensitivity to PARP inhibition in experimental BRCA-deficient systems. Cong 2021 studied single-stranded replication gaps in cellular models: gap suppression tracked resistance or resensitisation, while restoring fork protection did not always restore resistance in the tested models. Obstacle and gap explanations can coexist, but their relative contribution in a patient's tumour is not established by these experiments. A repair-gene variant alone does not reproduce the functional losses tested in a synthetic-lethal experiment.

points.heading: PARP inhibition creates another challenge
points.requirement: Some HR-deficient cells are especially vulnerable to that challenge, illustrating synthetic lethality. Experiments also show that catalytic inhibition and trapping strength can differ between compounds. Niraparib and olaparib trapped PARP more strongly than veliparib ([Murai 2012](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3528345/)), and talazoparib, a breast cancer PARP inhibitor, trapped about 100 times more potently than olaparib while inhibiting the enzyme similarly ([Murai 2014](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24356813/)). Laboratory trapping measurements do not rank the best medicine for a person. Exposure, normal-tissue effects, resistance, and clinical setting remain important. [The optional trapping lesson](/wiki/education/guides/from-variant-to-drug/04-parp-trapping-and-recycling) adds what can remove a trapped PARP.

Niraparib and olaparib trapped PARP more strongly than veliparib ([Murai 2012](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3528345/)), and talazoparib, a breast cancer PARP inhibitor, trapped about 100 times more potently than olaparib while inhibiting the enzyme similarly ([Murai 2014](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24356813/)). coverageEvidence.excerpt: Murai 2012 compared niraparib, olaparib and veliparib in defined cellular and biochemical systems: niraparib and olaparib trapped PARP-DNA complexes more strongly than veliparib, despite catalytic inhibition being a different comparison. coverageEvidence.excerpt:
Synthetic lethality is a lethal interaction between two impairments, each of which can be tolerated alone in the tested system. One impairment may already be present in a cancer and an experimental intervention can create the second, so the concept does not require two drugs. Genetic identity, loss of function, target engagement and the lethal outcome each need evidence.

The 2005 Farmer and Bryant studies found sensitivity to PARP inhibition in BRCA-impaired experimental systems. Murai and colleagues later distinguished PARP trapping from catalytic inhibition. These findings support particular mechanisms; they do not make every BRCA-related finding a clinical selection rule. Candidate pairs such as MTAP with PRMT5, mismatch-repair deficiency with WRN, or repair deficiency with POLQ need their own model, exposure, selectivity and clinical evidence.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
A repair-gene finding suggests a possible cause, a genomic scar records accumulated consequences, and a functional assay tests present behavior. A variant is not automatically damaging, loss of one copy is not automatically loss of both, and repair can recover while historical scars persist. None of these observations alone is the probability of clinical benefit.

Homologous recombination uses sufficiently matching DNA, often the sister chromatid after copying, to repair certain breaks. A low RAD51-focus count is interpretable only with adequate tumor cells, an appropriate cycling population and evidence that the cells experienced damage. Cruz 2018 assessed RAD51 with geminin as an S/G2 marker and gamma-H2AX as a damage marker in patient-derived models and retrospective tumor specimens. Fixed tissue can support this functional-surrogate approach; functional does not always mean live drug culture. An inadequate sample is uninformative, and a research assay needs analytical and clinical validation for its intended use.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A composite score can sum different scar features. coverageEvidence.excerpt: TBCRC 048 was a metastatic single-arm response study, a different question from adjuvant recurrence prevention. Tung's 2020 report enrolled 54 people with several germline or somatic repair-gene alterations; confirmed responses occurred with germline PALB2, 82 per cent, or somatic BRCA1/2, 50 per cent, in small subgroups, with no responses in ATM or CHEK2 alone. coverageEvidence.excerpt: For a repair-gene claim, keep the measured observation, method, source, supported conclusion and unresolved question together. Internal coherence means the findings fit a story but can share pipeline errors. Cross-report agreement can reuse a specimen or computation. Independent reproduction adds a separate auditable workflow with suitable controls without proving clinical utility. Clinical validation concerns the specified use and population, and does not guarantee an individual's response. These are different checks, not numerical confidence tiers. A credible DNA change, altered RNA junction, protein signal, current repair assay and model drug response each narrow a different gap; an old scar cannot vote away a present-function uncertainty. The route is a reading framework, not a mandatory research sequence or a validated treatment protocol.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a fictional report, laboratory X gives a score of 48 and a paper uses laboratory Y's cutoff of 42 in early triple-negative breast cancer. The numerical comparison 48 > 42 does not establish HRD positivity on X's assay: its scale, quality requirements and validated boundary are needed. Even on the correct scale, association with response to one regimen does not establish extra carboplatin benefit over a comparator. GeparSixto's interaction analysis and TNT's high-score result illustrate that distinction; neither permits a blanket claim that a high-score tumour never benefits from carboplatin.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
RAD51 nuclear foci are assemblies of a protein involved in homologous recombination. Their interpretation depends on the sampled tumour cells, cell-cycle state, damage, staining, scoring and controls. A low count without enough informative cycling cells is uninformative rather than proof that repair is absent. The assay is a functional surrogate, not direct observation of every completed repair event.

Cruz and colleagues in 2018 assessed RAD51 with geminin as an S/G2 marker and gamma-H2AX as a damage marker in patient-derived breast cancer models and retrospective tumour specimens. Castroviejo-Bermejo and colleagues separately compared RAD51 and genomic HRD scores against olaparib response in breast cancer xenografts, then assessed feasibility in archival breast samples, including PALB2-related cancers. The latter clinical samples established feasibility, rather than a randomised benefit from choosing treatment with the assay.

A scar records accumulated genomic changes; a suitably controlled RAD51 result asks about a present repair-related state. Repair-restoring changes and acquired foci were observed in selected resistant BRCA-mutated breast cancers, but those small cohorts do not establish a universal treatment-switch rule. Use the actual assay version, informative-cell requirements and intended-use validation. A research score cannot replace the biomarker, disease and companion-test conditions of a medicine's label.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a fictional repair-gene sequence, credible DNA evidence, an abnormal RNA junction and reduced staining in malignant cells progressively refine the question without becoming interchangeable measurements. The RNA result concerns captured transcripts. The stain concerns the antibody's detectable signal; determine which protein forms and epitopes the assay recognises before declaring intact functional protein absent. A controlled repair assay adds evidence at another level. Keep five claims separate: a real change, loss of both useful parental contributions, a compatible genomic history, impaired repair now, and benefit from treatment in the intended clinical setting. A coherent collection of markers is not a vote that turns all five claims into one label.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Enzyme assays and PAR immunoassays report catalytic activity or its product. NCI's PAR assay measures PAR levels in specified biospecimens; chromatin-associated PARP measurements instead investigate DNA retention under specified conditions. Matched genetic perturbations and appropriate controls are needed to distinguish reduced growth, reduced metabolism and loss of long-term survival.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A vehicle control contains the carrier without the active treatment; an untreated condition asks a different question if the carrier has effects. A positive control checks that the assay can detect a known relevant response, while a negative or non-targeting control estimates background under its design. Another independent way to disrupt the same function can support a mechanism, and a rescue restores a function to test whether that reverses the response here. Off-target effects, incomplete restoration and model context limit interpretation. These are questions for matched model, timing and readout; no one control proves specificity or patient benefit, and agreement between similar readouts is not automatically independent mechanistic confirmation.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Attribute each readout to the relevant cells. An ATP-based signal can change through cell number or per-cell metabolism, and slower single-cell mass accumulation does not by itself show death. Direct death measurements and regrowth after washout ask further questions; regrowth concerns surviving cells, not revival of cells already dead. A mixed culture can change composition, and a nonmalignant-cell label alone does not establish a validated healthy-tissue control. Ladan's breast-slice chemotherapy assay was compared with response during preoperative treatment in a defined setting. That assay-specific validation does not validate every postoperative combination, human exposure or clinical decision. An inadequate viable preparation should remain uninterpretable rather than be called resistant.

A credible DNA change, altered RNA junction, protein signal, current repair assay and model drug response each narrow a different gap; an old scar cannot vote away a present-function uncertainty. The route is a reading framework, not a mandatory research sequence or a validated treatment protocol.

points.heading: preamble
points.requirement: **A poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitor can both block an enzyme and leave a protein stuck to DNA. The cell's repair and clearance systems help determine what happens next.**

sourceRefs.exactPassage: **A poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitor can both block an enzyme and leave a protein stuck to DNA. The cell's repair and clearance systems help determine what happens next.**
**A poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitor can both block an enzyme and leave a protein stuck to DNA. The cell's repair and clearance systems help determine what happens next.**

points.entailment: Catalysis, retention, replication stress and clearance are different processes; the worker analogy is bounded.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: PARP means poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase, a protein family involved in cellular signalling and repair. PARP1 is one representative. At damaged DNA it can build signals on proteins from chains of the chemical unit ADP-ribose, called poly(ADP-ribose), or PAR. Catalytic inhibition reduces this output. Some inhibitors can also stabilise DNA-associated PARP complexes, often called trapping. A repair-worker analogy separates a reduced call for help from a worker remaining in a doorway; proteins and medicines have no purpose, and the cell has more than one response route.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A DNA-associated protein obstacle can challenge copying without every encounter becoming a measured collision, double-strand break or cell death. Farmer 2005 demonstrated increased sensitivity to PARP inhibition in experimental BRCA-deficient systems. Cong 2021 studied single-stranded replication gaps in cellular models: gap suppression tracked resistance or resensitisation, while restoring fork protection did not always restore resistance in the tested models. Obstacle and gap explanations can coexist, but their relative contribution in a patient's tumour is not established by these experiments. A repair-gene variant alone does not reproduce the functional losses tested in a synthetic-lethal experiment.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Hoslett and colleagues' 2026 preclinical study investigated selective disposal of trapped PARP1 involving TEX264, the protein-remodelling enzyme p97 and LC3-associated lysosomal handling. Autophagic handling of nuclear material is called nucleophagy. Perturbing the machinery increased chromatin-associated PARP1 and PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the studied systems; complementation and cargo-recognition experiments supported the proposed route. Some trapping experiments also supplied the DNA-damaging agent MMS, so their conditions are not every drug-alone exposure. The authors left the exact export or packaging of nuclear cargo, and macroautophagy versus direct microautophagy, unresolved. A clearance cartoon is therefore a mechanistic model, not established compartment geometry. Expression-survival associations do not validate TEX264 expression as a treatment-response test.

Homologous repair often uses the sister chromatid after DNA copying. The substrate, available template and cell-cycle state affect which route can operate.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
Synthetic lethality is a lethal interaction between two impairments, each of which can be tolerated alone in the tested system. One impairment may already be present in a cancer and an experimental intervention can create the second, so the concept does not require two drugs. Genetic identity, loss of function, target engagement and the lethal outcome each need evidence.

The 2005 Farmer and Bryant studies found sensitivity to PARP inhibition in BRCA-impaired experimental systems. Murai and colleagues later distinguished PARP trapping from catalytic inhibition. These findings support particular mechanisms; they do not make every BRCA-related finding a clinical selection rule. Candidate pairs such as MTAP with PRMT5, mismatch-repair deficiency with WRN, or repair deficiency with POLQ need their own model, exposure, selectivity and clinical evidence.

points.heading: The repair worker can become an obstacle
points.requirement: Trapping strength differs between compounds in a defined assay. Murai and colleagues found stronger trapping with niraparib and olaparib than with veliparib, despite all inhibiting PARP activity ([Murai 2012](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3528345/)). Talazoparib, used for germline-BRCA breast cancer, trapped PARP about 100 times more potently than olaparib while inhibiting the enzyme comparably ([Murai 2014](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24356813/)). This is a laboratory distinction. It does not rank the best drug for a person: exposure, toxicity, dose, resistance, and the clinical setting also matter.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Murai 2012 compared niraparib, olaparib and veliparib in defined cellular and biochemical systems: niraparib and olaparib trapped PARP-DNA complexes more strongly than veliparib, despite catalytic inhibition being a different comparison. Murai 2014 compared BMN673, now talazoparib, with olaparib and rucaparib. In damaged-DNA cell assays, 0.1 micromolar BMN673 produced a trapping signal comparable to 10 micromolar olaparib, about a 100-fold concentration difference; the purified DNA-binding assay gave a different, roughly 40-fold comparison. Similar catalytic effects did not imply similar trapping. Strongest among compounds tested in 2014 is not a ranking of clinical benefit, tolerated exposure or personal treatment choices.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: The Talzenna U.S. label effective October 2026 specifies adult breast-cancer use as a single agent for deleterious or suspected-deleterious germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic disease, selected with an FDA-authorised companion diagnostic. An unspecified germline variant is too broad. EMBRACA randomised 431 people with the trial's advanced HER2-negative germline-BRCA breast cancer to talazoparib or physician's-choice chemotherapy: median progression-free survival was 8.6 versus 5.6 months, hazard ratio 0.54. That clinical comparison is different from Murai's cell-assay trapping comparison with olaparib. Neither a laboratory potency ratio nor a cross-trial comparison establishes the best PARP inhibitor for an individual or an adjuvant indication.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Replication makes DNA from DNA. Transcription uses a DNA template to make RNA. Translation reads the coding sequence of a message in three-base codons to build a polypeptide; the transcript and reading frame matter. Functional noncoding RNAs do not need to become protein. Reverse transcription copies RNA into DNA in relevant viral and retrotransposon contexts. This information-flow map is not a guarantee that every DNA change produces a measured RNA or protein change.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A traceable finding identifies the specimen and assay, reference sequence with its version, genomic location and alleles, relevant transcript with its version, and supporting evidence. DNA means deoxyribonucleic acid and RNA means ribonucleic acid. A reference genome is the comparison sequence; a transcript is an RNA message. For a coding transcript, the annotated start codon fixes the coding frame, so the same genomic change can have different consequences in different transcripts. Not every transcript has a coding sequence. HGVS distinguishes experimentally observed RNA or protein changes from predicted consequences, conventionally putting predicted protein consequences in parentheses. A predicted splice effect is not a measured RNA junction, and a coordinate without its reference cannot safely join two reports.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Klionsky's 2021 assay guidelines distinguish LC3 carrier flux from actual cargo or substrate flux. LC3-II is the lipid-attached form of microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3; accumulation can reflect formation or slower removal. Compare treatment alone, a verified lysosomal block such as bafilomycin A1 alone, both together and the relevant baseline, with suitable time and dose windows. An additional LC3-II increase can support turnover under those conditions, but partial inhibition, saturation, low formation or cell death can complicate the comparison. Little change is not a unique diagnosis of an existing late block. A tandem two-colour reporter adds information about acidic delivery, not proof that every cargo completed degradation. Pair markers with an appropriate cargo measurement. Sequestosome 1, SQSTM1/p62, is an adaptor whose abundance also depends on expression and other processes, so one p62 snapshot cannot establish blockage.

points.heading: Flow still does not establish dependence
points.requirement: Published breast cancer experiments illustrate why both directions deserve attention. Bellare and colleagues found that disrupting autophagy increased talazoparib sensitivity in the HR-proficient models they studied. Arun and colleagues found that reducing ATG5, an autophagy machinery protein, partly reduced olaparib-induced apoptosis in the BRCA2-mutant HCC-1428 cell line, which is estrogen-receptor-positive rather than triple-negative ([Mouron 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33579347/)). **Apoptosis** is a regulated cell-death process. These studies used different models, drugs, and perturbations. Their results do not define a universal tumor label or individual treatment effect. [Bellare 2021](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8007595/), [Arun 2015](https://www.spandidos-publications.com/10.3892/ijo.2015.3003).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Breast-cancer studies illustrate the conditional direction. Bellare 2021 reported that genetic disruption or chloroquine increased talazoparib sensitivity in the tested HR-proficient cells and xenografts. Arun 2015 found that ATG5 reduction partly reduced olaparib-induced apoptosis in BRCA2-mutant HCC-1428 cells, an oestrogen-receptor-positive line rather than a triple-negative model. These different drugs, models and perturbations do not define one protective or death-promoting label for all tumours. Bellare's 2025 correction replaced representative MCF7 images in Figure 5c as well as a liver-histology image in Figure 6f. The authors stated that replicate-based quantification and interpretation were unchanged; that statement is theirs, not an independent validation of the replacement images.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A fictional one-hour recycling-station comparison starts with 20 waiting bags in each station. coverageEvidence.excerpt: PI3K means phosphoinositide 3-kinase; AKT is also called protein kinase B. Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, mTORC1, integrates growth and nutrient inputs. PTEN, phosphatase and tensin homolog, removes a phosphate from a PI3K-generated lipid signal. These protein and lipid reactions need their own readouts. coverageEvidence.excerpt:
EGFR, FGFR and FLT3 are examples of receptor tyrosine kinases. Their normal roles and activation arrangements differ across receptor families.

Receptor amount, phosphorylation, direct drug engagement, growth dependence and clinical benefit are separate observations. Lower receptor phosphorylation supports a biochemical effect under the assay conditions but can also reflect indirect regulation; it does not by itself prove direct binding. A controlled functional effect with independent specificity tests is needed before assigning receptor dependence.

Many RTKs have extracellular ligand-binding regions, membrane-spanning regions and intracellular tyrosine-kinase machinery. Families activate differently: Zhang demonstrated an asymmetric EGFR kinase-domain interaction, while Stauber examined an FGF1-FGFR2 extracellular complex with a proposed heparin-related assembly arrangement. Ligand, helper molecules, receptor member and context matter. A downstream phosphosite can have multiple upstream causes and is not a universal receptor meter.

Slamon 1987 studied 189 primary breast cancers and reported HER2 amplification in 30%, associated with relapse and survival; that historical study is not a present-day universal prevalence or a causal drug-response experiment. In the 2001 randomized trial of 469 women with HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer, adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy increased median survival from 20.3 to 25.1 months, with cardiac toxicity as a material risk. A trial median summarizes a group and does not predict an individual survival time.

In a fictional comparison, two cultures contain a receptor, but only the amplified, high-surface-protein culture slows growth after a blocking antibody, while receptor phosphorylation falls in both. This separates amount, sampled signaling and growth response; the pattern suggests dependence but attribution still needs controls and independent perturbation. RNA is not surface accessibility, a family-name inhibitor need not engage every member at the tested exposure. For an antibody-drug conjugate, receptor access and payload delivery are separate questions from whether growth requires that receptor's signaling. Fixed-tissue staining and viable-model perturbation have different input costs and validation scopes.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Replication makes DNA from DNA. Transcription uses a DNA template to make RNA. Translation reads the coding sequence of a message in three-base codons to build a polypeptide; the transcript and reading frame matter. Functional noncoding RNAs do not need to become protein. Reverse transcription copies RNA into DNA in relevant viral and retrotransposon contexts. This information-flow map is not a guarantee that every DNA change produces a measured RNA or protein change.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A traceable finding identifies the specimen and assay, reference sequence with its version, genomic location and alleles, relevant transcript with its version, and supporting evidence. DNA means deoxyribonucleic acid and RNA means ribonucleic acid. A reference genome is the comparison sequence; a transcript is an RNA message. For a coding transcript, the annotated start codon fixes the coding frame, so the same genomic change can have different consequences in different transcripts. Not every transcript has a coding sequence. HGVS distinguishes experimentally observed RNA or protein changes from predicted consequences, conventionally putting predicted protein consequences in parentheses. A predicted splice effect is not a measured RNA junction, and a coordinate without its reference cannot safely join two reports.

PDK1 phosphorylates AKT1 Thr308, whereas the rictor-mTOR complex supplies Ser473 phosphorylation in the defined experimental route. The diagram's indirect AKT-to-mTORC1 connection stands for these regulatory steps; it is not direct phosphorylation of mTORC1 by AKT.

Harrington linked S6K activity to reduced IRS-1 function, and O'Reilly observed increased IRS-1 and AKT signaling after RAD001 in cell models and treated tumors. Feedback release can change an output without proving that a combination improves outcomes in every setting.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Rapalogs, PI3K or AKT inhibitors and ATP-site mTOR kinase inhibitors are different interventions. In Rodrik-Outmezguine's 2011 models, inhibiting both mTOR complexes initially reduced AKT Ser473 and Thr308 phosphorylation, but relief of receptor feedback later restored Thr308 phosphorylation and AKT signalling while Ser473 remained suppressed. A Ser473 result therefore did not measure all AKT activity. O'Reilly's rapalog study and Harrington's IRS feedback work likewise explain why lower mTORC1 output can coexist with increased upstream signalling. These are measured responses in specified systems, not inevitable behaviour or a universal combination prescription.

points.heading: Follow the signal, then look for the brakes
points.requirement: A [**kinase**](/wiki/education/concepts/biology-basics/signaling/signal-transduction-and-kinases) adds phosphate groups to a target; a **phosphatase** removes them. The target may be a lipid or a protein. [Protein phosphorylation](/wiki/education/concepts/biology-basics/signaling/phosphorylation) can change activity without changing how much protein is present; the meaning depends on the measured site. RNA abundance alone cannot establish whether that restraint is working. [Maehama and Dixon 1998](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9593664/).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Many protein kinases transfer phosphate from ATP to selected substrate residues, commonly serine, threonine or tyrosine, leaving ADP. Protein amount is distinct from catalytic activity, and not every relay protein is a kinase. In the defined EGFR asymmetric-dimer mechanism, activation-loop phosphorylation was not required for activation.

points.heading: One intervention can affect two branches

points.heading: One intervention can affect two branches
points.requirement: The second branch concerns [autophagy](/wiki/education/concepts/cancer-biology/cell-death-and-survival/autophagy), the recycling process from [supporting lesson 5](./05-autophagy-flux-and-dependence). mTORC1 restrains machinery that starts this process. points.heading: Feedback can make neighboring signals disagree
points.requirement: Two named links explain the main loop. Going down, AKT phosphorylates **TSC2**, which disables the TSC complex; that complex normally switches off **RHEB**, a small GTPase that turns mTORC1 on. So AKT activates mTORC1 by releasing a brake on RHEB ([Inoki 2002](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12172553/); [Inoki 2003](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12869586/)). Coming back up, mTORC1 activates the kinase **S6K1**, which phosphorylates **IRS-1** (insulin receptor substrate 1), the adaptor that connects insulin and IGF-1 receptors to PI3K. That dampens the upstream signal.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Rapalogs, PI3K or AKT inhibitors and ATP-site mTOR kinase inhibitors are different interventions. In Rodrik-Outmezguine's 2011 models, inhibiting both mTOR complexes initially reduced AKT Ser473 and Thr308 phosphorylation, but relief of receptor feedback later restored Thr308 phosphorylation and AKT signalling while Ser473 remained suppressed. A Ser473 result therefore did not measure all AKT activity. O'Reilly's rapalog study and Harrington's IRS feedback work likewise explain why lower mTORC1 output can coexist with increased upstream signalling. These are measured responses in specified systems, not inevitable behaviour or a universal combination prescription.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Rapalogs, PI3K or AKT inhibitors and ATP-site mTOR kinase inhibitors are different interventions. In Rodrik-Outmezguine's 2011 models, inhibiting both mTOR complexes initially reduced AKT Ser473 and Thr308 phosphorylation, but relief of receptor feedback later restored Thr308 phosphorylation and AKT signalling while Ser473 remained suppressed. A Ser473 result therefore did not measure all AKT activity. O'Reilly's rapalog study and Harrington's IRS feedback work likewise explain why lower mTORC1 output can coexist with increased upstream signalling. coverageEvidence.excerpt: Klionsky's 2021 assay guidelines distinguish LC3 carrier flux from actual cargo or substrate flux. LC3-II is the lipid-attached form of microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3; accumulation can reflect formation or slower removal. Compare treatment alone, a verified lysosomal block such as bafilomycin A1 alone, both together and the relevant baseline, with suitable time and dose windows. An additional LC3-II increase can support turnover under those conditions, but partial inhibition, saturation, low formation or cell death can complicate the comparison. Little change is not a unique diagnosis of an existing late block. A tandem two-colour reporter adds information about acidic delivery, not proof that every cargo completed degradation. Pair markers with an appropriate cargo measurement. Sequestosome 1, SQSTM1/p62, is an adaptor whose abundance also depends on expression and other processes, so one p62 snapshot cannot establish blockage.

points.entailment: Repair and initiation branches can change together without determining survival; the Ibrahim and Kim findings remain model-specific.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: PI3K means phosphoinositide 3-kinase; AKT is also called protein kinase B. Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, mTORC1, integrates growth and nutrient inputs. PTEN, phosphatase and tensin homolog, removes a phosphate from a PI3K-generated lipid signal. These protein and lipid reactions need their own readouts. Ibrahim 2012 found that PI3K inhibition reduced BRCA1/2 expression and increased PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the BRCA-proficient triple-negative breast cancer models studied. A second branch concerns mTORC1 restraint of ULK1-associated autophagy initiation, studied by Kim 2011. Releasing an initiation brake does not establish completed cargo degradation or protective recycling. The two branches can change together without revealing the net survival effect. A model already lacking the relevant repair function cannot be assumed to gain the same vulnerability as one in which that function is newly reduced; measure protein and repair function, flux and survival under the actual compound, dose and schedule.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Rapalogs, PI3K or AKT inhibitors and ATP-site mTOR kinase inhibitors are different interventions. In Rodrik-Outmezguine's 2011 models, inhibiting both mTOR complexes initially reduced AKT Ser473 and Thr308 phosphorylation, but relief of receptor feedback later restored Thr308 phosphorylation and AKT signalling while Ser473 remained suppressed. A Ser473 result therefore did not measure all AKT activity. O'Reilly's rapalog study and Harrington's IRS feedback work likewise explain why lower mTORC1 output can coexist with increased upstream signalling. These are measured responses in specified systems, not inevitable behaviour or a universal combination prescription.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Klionsky's 2021 assay guidelines distinguish LC3 carrier flux from actual cargo or substrate flux. LC3-II is the lipid-attached form of microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3; accumulation can reflect formation or slower removal. Compare treatment alone, a verified lysosomal block such as bafilomycin A1 alone, both together and the relevant baseline, with suitable time and dose windows. An additional LC3-II increase can support turnover under those conditions, but partial inhibition, saturation, low formation or cell death can complicate the comparison. Little change is not a unique diagnosis of an existing late block. A tandem two-colour reporter adds information about acidic delivery, not proof that every cargo completed degradation. Pair markers with an appropriate cargo measurement. coverageEvidence.excerpt:
Synthetic lethality is a lethal interaction between two impairments, each of which can be tolerated alone in the tested system. One impairment may already be present in a cancer and an experimental intervention can create the second, so the concept does not require two drugs. Genetic identity, loss of function, target engagement and the lethal outcome each need evidence.

The 2005 Farmer and Bryant studies found sensitivity to PARP inhibition in BRCA-impaired experimental systems. Murai and colleagues later distinguished PARP trapping from catalytic inhibition. These findings support particular mechanisms; they do not make every BRCA-related finding a clinical selection rule. Candidate pairs such as MTAP with PRMT5, mismatch-repair deficiency with WRN, or repair deficiency with POLQ need their own model, exposure, selectivity and clinical evidence.

Regrowth after drug removal tests whether survivors can recover under the culture conditions. Measuring tumor-cell identity and composition helps establish which cells supplied the signal. A mixed culture may include nonmalignant cells, and culture can favor only some tumor populations.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Attribute each readout to the relevant cells. An ATP-based signal can change through cell number or per-cell metabolism, and slower single-cell mass accumulation does not by itself show death. Direct death measurements and regrowth after washout ask further questions; regrowth concerns surviving cells, not revival of cells already dead. A mixed culture can change composition, and a nonmalignant-cell label alone does not establish a validated healthy-tissue control. Ladan's breast-slice chemotherapy assay was compared with response during preoperative treatment in a defined setting. That assay-specific validation does not validate every postoperative combination, human exposure or clinical decision. An inadequate viable preparation should remain uninterpretable rather than be called resistant.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Keep what changed, the comparator, concentration or dose range, timing, assignment, readout and units, sample identities, replicate structure and variability. Repeated wells address variation under their preparation and allocation; independently obtained biological samples address another source of variation. Many wells from one tumour do not become independent patients, and repetition or a small p-value does not repair a missing comparison. A two-drug experiment needs vehicle, both single drugs and the combination. A larger combination effect than either single drug is not automatically synergy; that claim needs a stated reference model.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Ferroptosis involves iron-dependent membrane-lipid peroxidation and death. Cystine uptake through system xc- can support cysteine and glutathione availability; it does not transport glutathione itself. GPX4 uses glutathione to reduce lipid hydroperoxides, while FSP1 provides a parallel coenzyme-Q-associated defence. Dependence on these routes varies with the model and cellular conditions. Establishing the mechanism requires appropriately controlled measurements of death, lipid damage, iron dependence and rescue, with complementary perturbations. Findings in persistent or mesenchymal model cells do not establish a universal vulnerability or a treatment recommendation. Necrotic appearance, danger signals and adaptive antitumour immunity are separate questions.

points.entailment: Cargo/marker flux, trapped PARP and conditional RAD51 measurements match different proposed mechanisms.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Klionsky's 2021 assay guidelines distinguish LC3 carrier flux from actual cargo or substrate flux. LC3-II is the lipid-attached form of microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3; accumulation can reflect formation or slower removal. Compare treatment alone, a verified lysosomal block such as bafilomycin A1 alone, both together and the relevant baseline, with suitable time and dose windows. An additional LC3-II increase can support turnover under those conditions, but partial inhibition, saturation, low formation or cell death can complicate the comparison. Little change is not a unique diagnosis of an existing late block. A tandem two-colour reporter adds information about acidic delivery, not proof that every cargo completed degradation. Pair markers with an appropriate cargo measurement. Sequestosome 1, SQSTM1/p62, is an adaptor whose abundance also depends on expression and other processes, so one p62 snapshot cannot establish blockage.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: PARP means poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase, a protein family involved in cellular signalling and repair. PARP1 is one representative. At damaged DNA it can build signals on proteins from chains of the chemical unit ADP-ribose, called poly(ADP-ribose), or PAR. Catalytic inhibition reduces this output. Some inhibitors can also stabilise DNA-associated PARP complexes, often called trapping. A repair-worker analogy separates a reduced call for help from a worker remaining in a doorway; proteins and medicines have no purpose, and the cell has more than one response route.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
RAD51 nuclear foci are assemblies of a protein involved in homologous recombination. Their interpretation depends on the sampled tumour cells, cell-cycle state, damage, staining, scoring and controls. A low count without enough informative cycling cells is uninformative rather than proof that repair is absent. The assay is a functional surrogate, not direct observation of every completed repair event.

Cruz and colleagues in 2018 assessed RAD51 with geminin as an S/G2 marker and gamma-H2AX as a damage marker in patient-derived breast cancer models and retrospective tumour specimens. Castroviejo-Bermejo and colleagues separately compared RAD51 and genomic HRD scores against olaparib response in breast cancer xenografts, then assessed feasibility in archival breast samples, including PALB2-related cancers. The latter clinical samples established feasibility, rather than a randomised benefit from choosing treatment with the assay.

A scar records accumulated genomic changes; a suitably controlled RAD51 result asks about a present repair-related state. Repair-restoring changes and acquired foci were observed in selected resistant BRCA-mutated breast cancers, but those small cohorts do not establish a universal treatment-switch rule. Use the actual assay version, informative-cell requirements and intended-use validation. A research score cannot replace the biomarker, disease and companion-test conditions of a medicine's label.

points.heading: Ask what the readout actually measures
points.requirement: [Genetic dependency mapping](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/functional-models/dependency-mapping-crispr) tests specified genetic disruptions. An independent disruption of the proposed function can strengthen a causal claim, while leaving the drug's actual effects to be tested. Restoring that function in a **rescue experiment** can add further support. These are research methods, not features guaranteed by every drug screen. Autophagy assay guidelines are especially clear about combining appropriate measurements and controls. [Klionsky 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33634751/).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A vehicle control contains the carrier without the active treatment; an untreated condition asks a different question if the carrier has effects. A positive control checks that the assay can detect a known relevant response, while a negative or non-targeting control estimates background under its design. Another independent way to disrupt the same function can support a mechanism, and a rescue restores a function to test whether that reverses the response here. Off-target effects, incomplete restoration and model context limit interpretation. These are questions for matched model, timing and readout; no one control proves specificity or patient benefit, and agreement between similar readouts is not automatically independent mechanistic confirmation.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Bulk RNA abundance measures messages across the sampled cell mixture; it does not time cargo flow or establish dependence. ATG13 and FIP200 participate with ULK1 in initiation machinery, as Ganley 2009 studied, but an alteration in a component does not establish the direction of completed recycling. A mechanistic dependence test should measure the proposed change before extensive death alters the markers, combine complementary readouts, and where feasible perturb more than one autophagy gene at different steps. Klionsky's guidelines also caution that these proteins have other functions. Restoration and independent perturbations strengthen a specific causal explanation without making every genetic manipulation perfectly selective. A lower ATP or metabolic signal alone is neither counted death nor proof of autophagy dependence.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A rescue restores a proposed missing function or supply and tests whether a defined effect reverses. Adding a cake mix back after its removal implicates the mixture without identifying flour, sugar or another ingredient; likewise, broad mevalonate add-back does not isolate cholesterol. More specific branch perturbations and appropriate add-backs can narrow the explanation. Partial rescue can reflect incomplete delivery or restoration as well as additional contributors, so it does not prove a second cause. Place the add-back relative to the blocked step: supplying GGPP after an upstream synthesis block is different from inhibiting the transferase that uses GGPP, which the added substrate cannot simply be assumed to bypass. Include restoration-only and matched controls, verify the restored process and distinguish growth, morphology and death. A genetic perturbation also has its own specificity limits.

points.requirement: Suppose a fictional culture shows more death with a PARP inhibitor and a lysosomal drug. The first justified claim is a response in that culture at those exposures. If trapping, clearance, and controlled perturbation support the explanation, the lab may then argue for a mechanism in that model.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a fictional culture, more death with a PARP inhibitor plus a lysosomal drug fits several explanations: reduced clearance of trapped PARP, toxicity from the second drug itself, or another altered stress response. Measure chromatin-bound PARP1 over the relevant interval, include both single-drug conditions, and test the proposed clearance machinery with suitable independent perturbation and restoration. Unchanged trapped cargo despite more death argues against that particular clearance explanation. TEX264 or p97 perturbation is complementary evidence, not automatically perfectly selective, because proteins can have other functions. Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine alter lysosomal processes broadly. Survival alone, high recycling RNA or a broad lysosomal effect does not identify selective trapped-PARP disposal or establish patient benefit.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A fictional two-drug table normalises remaining viability to vehicle at 100 per cent: A leaves 70, B leaves 80, and combination examples leave 56 or 30. Highest single agent uses the better single-drug effect, a 70 per cent remaining-viability reference here. Bliss independence predicts 0.70 times 0.80 = 0.56, or 56 per cent. Both combinations exceed the HSA effect; 56 matches Bliss while 30 exceeds it at that dose pair. A further combination leaving 65 exceeds HSA but not Bliss. Loewe additivity instead needs equivalent-dose information from suitable individual dose-response curves; this one-point table cannot establish it. Report the model, dose-pair pattern, uncertainty and schedule. Interaction relative to a reference does not identify a biological mechanism, tolerable human exposure or a treatment choice.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Endpoint and validation example. Ladan reported 23 usable assays among 30 tumour-containing biopsies; three of the 23 did not proceed to the clinical treatment comparison, leaving 20 evaluable patients and 15 concordant MRI comparisons. The agreement compared sensitive, intermediate and resistant categories after four courses of anthracycline-containing chemotherapy; it is not a binary drug-killing rate. The study did not observe an ex vivo resistant group, limiting assessment of resistance detection. Those denominators, assay version and preoperative setting cannot validate another postoperative choice. Salmon measured matrix-associated T-cell location and movement in viable lung-tumour slices, not treatment-selection benefit.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Handling evidence is method-specific. Ladan and colleagues collected breast tissue in their specified medium, cut 300 micrometre slices and assessed morphology, proliferation and apoptosis after three-day exposure. This is not a general transport or storage protocol for all screens. Growth-rate methods show why baseline counts and control division affect interpretation. Retain failures and exclusions; failed preparation is not clinical resistance. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4887336/ Medium, drug access and exposure duration can change the result. Mechanism-relevant controls test whether the claimed interaction can occur; absent required cells or unrealistic exposures can make an experiment uninformative even when a numerical response is available. A laboratory concentration is not a safe human dose.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Restivo and colleagues generated organoids from matched fresh and slow-frozen colorectal tumour tissue from two patients with stage IV disease. Their specified slow-freezing protocol used a cryoprotectant to preserve living material, and the frozen-derived cultures took longer to form than the fresh-derived cultures. This is evidence of recovery under that protocol, not equivalence of all fresh, snap-frozen and viable-cryopreserved samples or a guaranteed turnaround. The handling history, recovery, malignant identity and assay quality need checking for the intended experiment. Preserved molecular material alone does not establish a recoverable living model. coverageEvidence.excerpt: A confirmation should test the suspected weakness. Check specimen identity and tissue, preparation, alteration class, usable local coverage, read quality and alignment; a high average depth does not establish adequate evidence at the disputed site. Reformatting one call or rerunning the same reads does not create independent molecular evidence. A separate preparation or a method with different relevant failure modes may help; a different brand name alone does not establish independence. In a fictional comparison, assay A reports a low-fraction variant and B reports none without site coverage. B has not disproved A. Request the exact site, usable local support, class-specific detection limit, specimen and time point. If both tests were adequate, reconcile the discrepancy, including sampling different populations or times, before building further interpretations.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Paired tumour and an appropriate nonmalignant comparator help attribute a finding. coverageEvidence.excerpt: Protection and dependence are experiment-specific directions. If removing a verified defence makes a defined stress more lethal, that supports protection under that stress. If removing the defence or a supply route reduces survival relative to an appropriate matched comparison, that supports a conditional dependence; it need not mean every unstressed cell dies. In a fictional culture, high antioxidant RNA plus probe-associated death establishes neither NRF2-driven killing nor ferroptosis. Test the alteration's effect on NRF2 turnover or nuclear localisation and output, then use independent perturbation and restoration to examine the survival mechanism. CUL3 works with other adaptors, and a compound suppressing protein production broadly does not isolate NRF2. A genetic intervention also needs controls, rather than being automatically specific.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Hoslett and colleagues' 2026 preclinical study investigated selective disposal of trapped PARP1 involving TEX264, the protein-remodelling enzyme p97 and LC3-associated lysosomal handling. coverageEvidence.excerpt: PI3K means phosphoinositide 3-kinase; AKT is also called protein kinase B. Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, mTORC1, integrates growth and nutrient inputs. PTEN, phosphatase and tensin homolog, removes a phosphate from a PI3K-generated lipid signal. These protein and lipid reactions need their own readouts. Ibrahim 2012 found that PI3K inhibition reduced BRCA1/2 expression and increased PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the BRCA-proficient triple-negative breast cancer models studied. A second branch concerns mTORC1 restraint of ULK1-associated autophagy initiation, studied by Kim 2011. Releasing an initiation brake does not establish completed cargo degradation or protective recycling. The two branches can change together without revealing the net survival effect. A model already lacking the relevant repair function cannot be assumed to gain the same vulnerability as one in which that function is newly reduced; measure protein and repair function, flux and survival under the actual compound, dose and schedule.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A rescue restores a proposed missing function or supply and tests whether a defined effect reverses. Adding a cake mix back after its removal implicates the mixture without identifying flour, sugar or another ingredient; likewise, broad mevalonate add-back does not isolate cholesterol. More specific branch perturbations and appropriate add-backs can narrow the explanation. Partial rescue can reflect incomplete delivery or restoration as well as additional contributors, so it does not prove a second cause. Place the add-back relative to the blocked step: supplying GGPP after an upstream synthesis block is different from inhibiting the transferase that uses GGPP, which the added substrate cannot simply be assumed to bypass. Include restoration-only and matched controls, verify the restored process and distinguish growth, morphology and death. A genetic perturbation also has its own specificity limits.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Stoeck 2014 identified NOTCH1 or NOTCH2 rearrangements in six of 66 triple-negative breast cancers. The studied NOTCH1 rearrangements retained gamma-secretase-dependent release of the active intracellular domain, and high-active-NOTCH1 models responded to inhibition in culture and xenografts, including tested paclitaxel combinations. A NOTCH2 fusion encoded an active intracellular product that bypassed the cleavage step and its model resisted that inhibitor. Position alone was not sufficient: a NOTCH1-rearranged line with low active-NOTCH1 signal also resisted. Both the actual active product and model conditions matter. The experiment does not make all activated Notch equivalent, validate a universal staining cutoff or establish a clinical selection rule.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a fictional paired-well example, culture A uses 180 picomoles of oxygen per minute with 30,000 viable cells and B uses 120 with 20,000. Both equal 60 per minute per 10,000 viable cells. After ATP-synthase blockade their corresponding normalised rates are 30 and 40, giving inhibitor-sensitive differences of 30 and 20 picomoles of oxygen per minute per 10,000 cells. coverageEvidence.excerpt: A traceable finding identifies the specimen and assay, reference sequence with its version, genomic location and alleles, relevant transcript with its version, and supporting evidence. DNA means deoxyribonucleic acid and RNA means ribonucleic acid. A reference genome is the comparison sequence; a transcript is an RNA message. For a coding transcript, the annotated start codon fixes the coding frame, so the same genomic change can have different consequences in different transcripts. Not every transcript has a coding sequence. HGVS distinguishes experimentally observed RNA or protein changes from predicted consequences, conventionally putting predicted protein consequences in parentheses. A predicted splice effect is not a measured RNA junction, and a coordinate without its reference cannot safely join two reports.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Sequencing and functional testing answer different questions. A tissue or plasma assay needs coverage around the original variant, suitable deletion and splice-change detection, and a way to assess whether the changes share an allele; a hotspot-only panel can miss such events. A negative-foci sample with too few proliferating cells was uninterpretable. A visible focus alone does not establish completed repair, and a single RAD51 method cannot substitute for all sequence and clinical evidence.

points.heading: PARP inhibition creates another challenge
points.requirement: Some HR-deficient cells are especially vulnerable to that challenge, illustrating synthetic lethality. Experiments also show that catalytic inhibition and trapping strength can differ between compounds. Niraparib and olaparib trapped PARP more strongly than veliparib ([Murai 2012](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3528345/)). In cell-based assays, talazoparib, which is approved as a single agent for HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer with a germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 variant ([talazoparib label](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=f2423edd-6d24-495c-aec1-c2f457f08d9a)), trapped PARP about 100 times more potently than olaparib while inhibiting the enzyme comparably ([Murai 2014](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24356813/)). coverageEvidence.excerpt:
Synthetic lethality is a lethal interaction between two impairments, each of which can be tolerated alone in the tested system. One impairment may already be present in a cancer and an experimental intervention can create the second, so the concept does not require two drugs. Genetic identity, loss of function, target engagement and the lethal outcome each need evidence.

The 2005 Farmer and Bryant studies found sensitivity to PARP inhibition in BRCA-impaired experimental systems. Murai and colleagues later distinguished PARP trapping from catalytic inhibition. These findings support particular mechanisms; they do not make every BRCA-related finding a clinical selection rule. Candidate pairs such as MTAP with PRMT5, mismatch-repair deficiency with WRN, or repair deficiency with POLQ need their own model, exposure, selectivity and clinical evidence.

Bortezomib's relapsed-myeloma trial result does not predict a hydroxychloroquine result in pancreatic cancer, and blocking both routes does not by itself demonstrate selective harm to malignant cells.

points.heading: Count bags, then watch the trucks
points.requirement: Think of a recycling station. A photograph showing many bags could mean many deliveries are arriving. It could also mean the trucks stopped leaving. The photograph alone does not tell you how much material completes its trip.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A fictional one-hour recycling-station comparison starts with 20 waiting bags in each station. A receives 30 and processes 30, leaving 20; B receives five and processes none, leaving 25. Equal initial piles, including a six-bag schematic snapshot, cannot identify the rate or the later outcome. Bags are not LC3 molecules or assay thresholds: real markers are produced and removed, cargos differ, and a perturbation can affect several steps. Measure completion over time with appropriate controls. Even verified flow does not establish survival dependence; after a specific perturbation, more death can support a protective role, less drug-induced death can support a contribution to that death response, and changed flow with similar survival leaves timing or compensation as possible limits.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Bulk RNA abundance measures messages across the sampled cell mixture; it does not time cargo flow or establish dependence. ATG13 and FIP200 participate with ULK1 in initiation machinery, as Ganley 2009 studied, but an alteration in a component does not establish the direction of completed recycling. A mechanistic dependence test should measure the proposed change before extensive death alters the markers, combine complementary readouts, and where feasible perturb more than one autophagy gene at different steps. Klionsky's guidelines also caution that these proteins have other functions. Restoration and independent perturbations strengthen a specific causal explanation without making every genetic manipulation perfectly selective. A lower ATP or metabolic signal alone is neither counted death nor proof of autophagy dependence.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Klionsky's 2021 assay guidelines distinguish LC3 carrier flux from actual cargo or substrate flux. LC3-II is the lipid-attached form of microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3; accumulation can reflect formation or slower removal. Compare treatment alone, a verified lysosomal block such as bafilomycin A1 alone, both together and the relevant baseline, with suitable time and dose windows. An additional LC3-II increase can support turnover under those conditions, but partial inhibition, saturation, low formation or cell death can complicate the comparison. Little change is not a unique diagnosis of an existing late block. A tandem two-colour reporter adds information about acidic delivery, not proof that every cargo completed degradation. Pair markers with an appropriate cargo measurement. Sequestosome 1, SQSTM1/p62, is an adaptor whose abundance also depends on expression and other processes, so one p62 snapshot cannot establish blockage.

Expert guidelines recommend combining complementary measurements rather than relying on one static marker [2].

points.heading: Two disposal routes, two kinds of cargo
points.requirement: Cells have a second disposal system. The **ubiquitin–proteasome** route tags individual proteins, often short-lived regulators, with ubiquitin chains and shreds them in a barrel-shaped protease. Autophagy handles bulk material: protein clumps, damaged organelles and portions of the cytoplasm, which it delivers to lysosomes. The routes interact; p62, for example, links ubiquitin-tagged cargo to autophagic membranes. But they have different machinery and different drugs:

sourceRefs.exactPassage: Cells have a second disposal system. The **ubiquitin–proteasome** route tags individual proteins, often short-lived regulators, with ubiquitin chains and shreds them in a barrel-shaped protease. Autophagy handles bulk material: protein clumps, damaged organelles and portions of the cytoplasm, which it delivers to lysosomes. The routes interact; p62, for example, links ubiquitin-tagged cargo to autophagic membranes. But they have different machinery and different drugs:

points.entailment: Typical proteasomal and autophagy cargo/machinery differ while ubiquitin/adaptor interactions can overlap.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Proteasomal degradation commonly handles individual suitable proteins, whereas lysosomal macroautophagy can deliver aggregates, organelles and portions of cytoplasm. This is a distinction of machinery and typical cargo, not an absolute partition: ubiquitinated material can also be recognised by autophagy adaptors such as p62. A tagged protein, an autophagic membrane marker and disappearance of a named cargo are different observations. Bortezomib's relapsed-myeloma trial result does not predict a hydroxychloroquine result in pancreatic cancer, and blocking both routes does not by itself demonstrate selective harm to malignant cells.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Ubiquitin is a small protein attached through enzyme steps: E1 uses ATP for activation, E2 carries activated ubiquitin, and E3 promotes substrate selection and transfer. Reticulocyte experiments separated these functions. E3 families differ in transfer mechanism; no single cartoon specifies all of them.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Suitable tagged cargo can be unfolded by ATP-dependent proteasomal machinery and broken into fragments, while ubiquitin is removed and reused. Other ubiquitin signals organise interactions rather than destruction, and yeast experiments show overlapping chain functions. Lysosomal autophagy and proteasomal breakdown are distinct routes.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Macroautophagy encloses cargo in a double-membrane autophagosome, delivers it through lysosomal fusion and degrades it for reuse. Formation, delivery and breakdown are separate steps; not all lysosomal processes use autophagosomes. Active recycling often supports stress adaptation, whereas autophagy-dependent death requires causal evidence implicating the machinery.

Survival alone, high recycling RNA or a broad lysosomal effect does not identify selective trapped-PARP disposal or establish patient benefit.

points.heading: Flow still does not establish dependence
points.requirement: Published breast cancer experiments show why both directions deserve attention. Bellare and colleagues found that blocking autophagy, genetically or with chloroquine, increased sensitivity to the PARP inhibitor talazoparib in HR-proficient breast cancer cells and mouse models [5]. Arun and colleagues found that reducing ATG5, an autophagy machinery protein, partly reduced olaparib-induced apoptosis, a regulated cell-death process, in the BRCA2-mutant HCC-1428 cell line [6], which is estrogen-receptor-positive rather than triple-negative [7]. These studies used different models, drugs and perturbations. Read Bellare's report with its [2025 correction](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40527957/), which replaced an incorrectly assembled liver-histology image in Figure 6f.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Breast-cancer studies illustrate the conditional direction. Bellare 2021 reported that genetic disruption or chloroquine increased talazoparib sensitivity in the tested HR-proficient cells and xenografts. Arun 2015 found that ATG5 reduction partly reduced olaparib-induced apoptosis in BRCA2-mutant HCC-1428 cells, an oestrogen-receptor-positive line rather than a triple-negative model. points.heading: One intervention can affect two branches
points.requirement: The second branch concerns [autophagy](/wiki/education/concepts/cancer-biology/cell-death-and-survival/autophagy), the recycling process from [lesson 5](/wiki/education/guides/from-variant-to-drug/05-autophagy-flux-and-dependence). mTORC1 restrains machinery that starts this process. Reducing that restraint can make initiation easier. It does not show that cargo completes degradation or that the increased recycling helps the cell survive. Those are separate measurements. Experiments connecting mTORC1 to the initiation protein ULK1 support this control mechanism. ULK1 is a kinase involved in starting autophagy. coverageEvidence.excerpt: PI3K means phosphoinositide 3-kinase; AKT is also called protein kinase B. Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, mTORC1, integrates growth and nutrient inputs. PTEN, phosphatase and tensin homolog, removes a phosphate from a PI3K-generated lipid signal. These protein and lipid reactions need their own readouts. Ibrahim 2012 found that PI3K inhibition reduced BRCA1/2 expression and increased PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the BRCA-proficient triple-negative breast cancer models studied. A second branch concerns mTORC1 restraint of ULK1-associated autophagy initiation, studied by Kim 2011. Releasing an initiation brake does not establish completed cargo degradation or protective recycling. The two branches can change together without revealing the net survival effect. A model already lacking the relevant repair function cannot be assumed to gain the same vulnerability as one in which that function is newly reduced; measure protein and repair function, flux and survival under the actual compound, dose and schedule.

points.heading: Feedback can make neighboring signals disagree
points.requirement: Two named links explain the main loop. Going down, AKT phosphorylates **TSC2**, which disables the TSC complex; that complex normally switches off **RHEB**, a small GTPase that turns mTORC1 on. So AKT activates mTORC1 by releasing a brake on RHEB ([Inoki 2002](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12172553/); [Inoki 2003](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12869586/)). Coming back up, mTORC1 activates the kinase **S6K1**, which phosphorylates **IRS-1** (insulin receptor substrate 1), the adaptor that connects the insulin and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) receptors to PI3K. That dampens the upstream signal ([Harrington 2004](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15249583/)).

The diagram's indirect AKT-to-mTORC1 connection stands for these regulatory steps; it is not direct phosphorylation of mTORC1 by AKT.
